nodes.label: Captured Init payload (data/init_0.6.3.json, createcar_summer1.json)
nodes.rationale: polyrl's physics_assets.json is off by one float32 ULP on 164 of 186 parts and the car hull; with it only 2 of 27 recordings verify. Always boot from the Init captured from the real client. Kodub's geometry; do not redistribute.

nodes.label: rl/: reinforcement learning on the headless simulator
nodes.norm_label: rl/: reinforcement learning on the headless simulator
nodes.rationale: Scaffolding only: working plumbing and a training loop, not a trained agent. Local use only; no network connections; bot laps must never be submitted.

nodes.label: Windows git autocrlf rewrites vendored worker bundle
nodes.norm_label: windows git autocrlf rewrites vendored worker bundle
nodes.rationale: autocrlf rewrites the vendored worker bundle and breaks hash checks, so npm run setup clones with it off.

nodes.label: Eager pump loop in worker entry
nodes.norm_label: eager pump loop in worker entry
nodes.rationale: The stock non-realtime loop polls on a timer, costing about 9 ms per step call on Windows; running the same loop eagerly gives about 52,000 frames/s at 10 frames per call.

nodes.label: Local-only policy: never submit bot laps
nodes.norm_label: local-only policy: never submit bot laps
nodes.rationale: Nothing talks to Kodub's leaderboard server; bot runs are for local ghosts only. The client uploads any stored lap that beats the server's copy, so bot recordings must never go into localStorage in a normal browser; watch_ghost uses a temporary Edge profile with vps.kodub.com blocked.

nodes.label: Mountains / backdrop terrain omission
nodes.rationale: Mountains made no difference on summer1 or winter1. Tracks without a capture run with none, which is only safe if the car cannot reach the backdrop terrain.

nodes.label: Controller settings tuning (crossTrackGain, airBrake)
nodes.rationale: summer1: human 22.279 s, baseline 23.835 s, tuned 22.403 s (holding brake in the air). winter1: human 17.011 s, tuned 17.048 s, started from crossTrackGain=2 airBrake=1 because the defaults do not finish.

nodes.label: Episode end: finish, stall, off-line distance, tick limit
nodes.norm_label: episode end: finish, stall, off-line distance, tick limit

nodes.label: Observation: 146 numbers scaled to about -1..1
nodes.rationale: 21 car values, 60 for the next 20 reference-line points in the car's frame, 20 human speeds at those points, the rest road-edge distances and key state. Speed scaling assumes about 300 km/h; winter1 reaches about 400, values are clipped at 3.

nodes.label: Actions: 12 key combinations (W x S x steer)
nodes.norm_label: actions: 12 key combinations (w x s x steer)
nodes.rationale: W and S can be held together because humans do that over every jump. Steering chosen every 10 ms; W and S every 50 ms and held, with a small reward cost per key press/release so keys are held rather than tapped. The network makes the three choices separately.

nodes.label: --no-lap-fraction (hide lap-progress input)
nodes.rationale: Hides the lap-fraction input so the agent cannot memorise a track by position.

nodes.label: Starts part-way round (--random-start)
nodes.rationale: Without part-way starts the agent can only practise a corner after surviving all the ones before it. The start point is reached by replaying the human's keys, which slows training. Evaluation always starts on the start line.

nodes.label: Reward: progress along reference line plus finish bonus
nodes.norm_label: reward: progress along reference line plus finish bonus
nodes.rationale: 0.1 per unit gained along the reference line, and 5 + 2 per second left on finishing. Every finished lap collects the same progress reward, so the faster of two finished laps always has the larger total.

nodes.label: Imitation first (behaviour cloning of top human laps)
nodes.norm_label: imitation first (behaviour cloning of top human laps)

nodes.label: What was not tested
nodes.rationale: No real training run; whether the settings reach a finished lap is unknown. evaluate.py with a trained policy, the Gymnasium code path, and --device cuda are untested.

nodes.label: gymnasium>=0.29 (optional)
nodes.rationale: Optional: if installed, PolytrackEnv becomes a real gymnasium.Env with observation_space/action_space so libraries such as Stable-Baselines3 can use it. Nothing in rl/ needs it.

nodes.label: torch>=2.2
nodes.rationale: Required for train_ppo.py and for evaluate.py with a trained policy. The CPU build is enough; the networks are small.

nodes.label: PPO (hand-written in PyTorch)
nodes.rationale: PPO suits a small discrete action set and many parallel environments and is stable with little tuning. Hand-written rather than Stable-Baselines3 because torch was already installed and SB3/Gymnasium were not, and a single commented file is easier to follow and change.

nodes.label: 227-byte car state per 1 ms tick
nodes.rationale: The state buffer is variable-length and reused, so bytes past stateLength() are stale; compare or hash only the written prefix.

nodes.label: test:determinism (same state stream across processes and replay vs live)
nodes.norm_label: test:determinism (same state stream across processes and replay vs live)

nodes.label: JSON-lines stdin/stdout protocol (reset, step, save, close)
nodes.norm_label: json-lines stdin/stdout protocol (reset, step, save, close)
nodes.rationale: Known limit: eight environments give about 3x one environment's speed through Python because the client reads JSON replies one after another; a binary protocol or more ticks per decision would help.

nodes.label: Server-side rollout command
nodes.rationale: Each process runs the policy itself for a whole batch and reports back once, avoiding a per-step round trip; the trainer writes weights to <checkpoint>.actor.bin before every batch.

nodes.label: Scoring laps in separate processes
nodes.rationale: Simulator threads inside one Node process do not scale past about two, so the search scores laps in separate processes.

nodes.label: Collection throughput measurements
nodes.rationale: About 5,700 decisions/s with 256-wide layers, 3,500 with 512-wide: the policy's own arithmetic in JavaScript costs more than the physics. 14 processes are only about 2.7x faster than one and 28 are slower, since each process keeps two threads busy and 8 cores are oversubscribed.
